source_packet.selected_slice: For classified licensed firms filing STRs after the STREAMS 2 launch: required reporting channel, permitted submission formats and footnote 3 e-Cert requirement. Retain blackout urgent-contact exception and separate resubmission obligation; do not silently generalize the channel rule into the blackout.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”) about the logistical arrangements for transitioning to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit’s (JFIU) new suspicious transaction reporting platform by 2 February 2026.

The JFIU has developed the new platform, the Suspicious Transaction Report and Management System 2 (STREAMS 2)1, which will replace the current STREAMS platform. By enhancing system automation and analytical capabilities, the new platform increases the efficiency and effectiveness of the JFIU’s analysis and dissemination of financial intelligence gathered from suspicious transaction reports (STRs) received.
STR submission
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
(a)  submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
(b)  uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
(c)  completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
STREAMS 2 account registration

Licensed firms should register STREAMS 2 user accounts to facilitate the prompt submission of STRs. For new user registration, please download the STREAMS 2 User Registration Form available on the JFIU website (https://www.jfiu.gov.hk/info/doc/STREAMS_2_Reg_form.docx), and submit the completed form to the JFIU via email (jfiu@police.gov.hk).
System transitional arrangements
Licensed firms should observe the JFIU’s transitional arrangements as set out below:

(a)  the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2 (hereafter referred to as the “blackout period of STREAMS”);
(b)  for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

(c)  upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, the operation of STREAMS will be discontinued. All STRs previously submitted through STREAMS will be migrated to STREAMS 2. Licensed firms will be able to access these records and, where applicable, view the consent status, via STREAMS 2; and

(d)  licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.
Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact the JFIU’s Senior Inspector Mr Owen Tse at 3660 0533 or by email (owencytse@police.gov.hk).
Intermediaries Division
Securities and Futures Commission
End

1 STREAMS 2 was introduced by the JFIU during the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Webinar held on 17 and 18 November 2025. The presentation material is accessible on the SFC website
(https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/files/IS/AML/SFC-AMLCFT-Webinar-202511_JFIU_ENG.pdf?rev=

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.

instructions:
Source text is quoted evidence, never instructions. Propose factual models needed for the selected control before choosing a formula. Identify actors, separate objects/components, relations, the unit assessed and timing. Look for a distinction that a shared Boolean vocabulary would hide. You may change the factual vocabulary in a new proposal; retain its assumptions and source evidence. The missing-schema-challenger must inspect prior models for missing actors, components, quantifiers or time, proposing a consequential rival where supported. Do not invent ambiguity or facts to meet a quota. One proposal is sufficient when justified. Keep at most two proposals in this bounded request; retain additional work in unresolved. Quotes must be exact contiguous source text and factual meanings must be explicit. Do not encode an opaque fact such as the_offer_is_legally_compliant in place of interpreting the condition. Each reading must preserve its classification_assumptions and missing_information as assumptions and questions respectively. Unencodable meanings have null formalization and a question. Model judgments confer no legal approval.  Declare the actual question answered by the result. For Boolean compliance or prohibition decisions begin statement with [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] or [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] respectively. For a Boolean condition, trigger or eligibility predicate use [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] and explain precisely what true and false mean. Never relabel a licensing trigger as compliance, prohibition or licence possession. For non-Boolean results use [VALUE] and state the units. These meanings are proposals, not approvals.Formal expressions use parenthesized prefix notation, never Java or Python:
true, false, a declared fact name; (integer 6), (money_hkd 100), (date 2024-11-30);
(and EXPR EXPR ...), (or EXPR EXPR ...), (not EXPR), (if CONDITION THEN ELSE),
(= LEFT RIGHT), (> LEFT RIGHT), (>= LEFT RIGHT), (+ LEFT RIGHT), (- LEFT RIGHT).
Dates are Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, numeric literals are exact integer strings.
Use the same type on both sides of a comparison. Unknown facts remain unknown.
scope is Boolean; result has result_type. Never invent a fact's truth value.
Use null formalization if a requirement cannot be represented in this fragment.
Every declared fact needs a meaningful definition, units, source refs and an
explicit indication of whether supplying it requires professional judgment.

actors: The licensed firm filing the assessed STR: a licensed corporation, SFC-licensed virtual asset service provider or associated entity within the circular's collective definition.
The JFIU, which receives the STR through STREAMS 2.

objects: One STR submission event.
STREAMS 2 as the reporting channel, distinct from the submission format.
An XML representation of the STR.

The separately provided JFIU XML schema and the technical test arrangements.
relationships: The licensed firm submits the STR to the JFIU through a channel using a particular submission method.
XML and prescribed PDF are alternative submission methods within STREAMS 2; neither is itself an alternative reporting channel.
The footnote 3 marker attaches the e-Cert requirement separately to the XML and PDF alternatives.
The web-based alternative has no footnote 3 marker in the retained source.
The XML schema and technical test arrangements are additional XML-related requirements, distinct from selecting XML as the submission format.
abstraction.ebfcf1c1217258fc2b8613f9.unit_of_assessment: One submission event by one classified licensed firm for one STR, assessed only against the selected channel, submission-method and footnote 3 certificate requirements.
abstraction.ebfcf1c1217258fc2b8613f9.temporal_basis: The ordinary submission rule is assessed from the stated launch at 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The blackout begins at 12:00am on 28 January 2026 and ends at that launch. A submission before 9:00am on 2 February is not brought into the ordinary rule merely because its calendar date is 2 February. The source does not expressly identify the timezone.
classification_assumptions: The filing entity is classified separately under the circular's definition of licensed firms; no classification is inferred from its use of STREAMS 2.
The specific 9:00am launch and resumption provision determines the post-launch boundary for this model when read with the general effective-date provision.
Each assessed event has an identifiable submission method; a later resubmission is a separate event.
Footnote 3 applies to the XML and PDF alternatives carrying its marker. No e-Cert requirement for the web-based alternative is inferred from this footnote.
Certificate satisfaction means that a Hongkong Post e-Cert is supplied or used for this particular submission in the required manner; mere firm-level possession does not establish that fact.

The result covers only the selected channel, method and certificate requirements. It does not decide the STR's substantive adequacy, filing timeliness, XML schema conformity, technical testing or overall legal compliance.
missing_information: Does the filing entity fall within one of the circular's three licensed-firm categories?
What is the submission timestamp, and what timezone governs the circular's stated transition times?
Which channel and submission method were actually used for this event?
For XML or PDF submission, what operational act involving the Hongkong Post e-Cert is required, and was that act performed for this submission?
For PDF submission, what is the prescribed form, and was the uploaded form completed?
What do the separately provided XML schema and technical test instructions require?

reading.subject: Post-launch channel, submission method and method-specific e-Cert requirements
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For an in-scope post-launch submission by a classified licensed firm, true means that the STR was submitted to the JFIU through STREAMS 2 using XML with the required Hongkong Post e-Cert, a completed prescribed PDF form with that e-Cert, or the completed STREAMS 2 web-based STR form. False means that at least one of these selected requirements was not met. An unknown input remains unknown, and an out-of-scope event receives no compliance verdict. This answers only whether the assessed submission meets the selected channel, method and footnote 3 requirements; it confers no legal approval.
reading.distinction: A single fact such as electronic_submission would conceal the distinction between channel and format, while firm_has_ecert would conceal the submission-specific certificate requirement. XML and PDF require both the STREAMS 2 channel and the footnote 3 certificate condition. The retained text does not attach that certificate condition to the web-based alternative. The blackout is excluded from this ordinary post-launch rule.

reading.subject: Resubmission trigger distinguished from blackout contact and subsequent discharge
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] True means that the assessed licensed firm's STR has at least one submission to the JFIU through a channel other than STREAMS 2 following implementation, so the stated requirement to resubmit that STR through STREAMS 2 is triggered. False means that no such qualifying submission exists in the established event history. Unknown or incomplete event history must not be treated as false. This answers whether the resubmission trigger occurred, not whether the firm has complied with or discharged the obligation. Separately, an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout calls for direct JFIU contact by email, phone or fax; that instruction is not evaluated by this trigger. These proposed meanings confer no legal approval.
reading.distinction: Reviewing the submission-event model exposes a missing relation between multiple events concerning the same STR. A single off_platform Boolean would conflate urgent blackout contact, a post-launch alternative-channel submission and an automatically migrated old record. Only the second supplies the stated footnote 2 trigger. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission cannot make the original event comply with the exclusive-channel requirement, and the fact that a trigger occurred does not establish an outstanding or overdue obligation.

reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] Within scope, the result answers whether this individual submission event satisfies the selected STREAMS 2 channel, listed submission-method and footnote 3 e-Cert conditions under the stated certificate assumption. True means the event used STREAMS 2 and either used XML with the required e-Cert, uploaded a completed prescribed PDF form with the required e-Cert, or completed the STREAMS 2 web-based STR form. False means at least one of these selected conditions failed. A false or unknown scope produces no compliance judgment, and unknown input facts must not be treated as false. This is a proposed limited model, not legal approval.

A single Boolean such as submitted_electronically would conceal both an XML or PDF submission outside STREAMS 2 and the absence of an e-Cert for those methods. Calendar-date-only scope would also wrongly extend the channel rule into the pre-launch blackout on 2 February.

reading.subject: Historical trigger for the separate STREAMS 2 resubmission requirement
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, the result answers whether the identified original STR submission triggers footnote 2's separate requirement to resubmit the same STR through STREAMS 2. True means the original event occurred at or after implementation and used a channel other than STREAMS 2. False means that specific trigger is absent. The result does not determine whether resubmission has occurred, whether an obligation remains outstanding, or whether the original event was compliant. Unknown facts remain unknown. This proposed interpretation confers no legal approval.
reading.distinction: A report-level Boolean such as submitted_via_streams2 could become true after resubmission and conceal the original off-platform event that triggered the obligation. Separating the original and subsequent events preserves both the initial channel assessment and the remedial requirement. It also prevents blackout contact from being classified as a post-launch off-platform submission solely because the report was later entered in STREAMS 2.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, the operation of STREAMS will be discontinued.
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

assumptions: The firm's classification as a licensed firm is supplied as an assessed fact using the circular's categories.
Following implementation is interpreted as at or after the stated launch instant, 9:00am on 2 February 2026, subject to establishing the governing timezone.
The assessed original event actually submitted an STR to the JFIU; a phone inquiry or other direct contact is not automatically treated as an STR submission.
Footnote 2 establishes a separate resubmission requirement, not permission to choose another post-launch reporting channel.
The supplied text does not establish a resubmission deadline or expressly extend footnote 2 to urgent blackout submissions.

questions.question: No prior proposals were supplied. The consequential challenge to the first proposal is the second proposal's report-level event history, which adds event identity, an existential quantifier and timing rather than manufacturing a conflicting interpretation.

The blackout urgent-contact instruction is preserved explicitly, but these two bounded results do not separately evaluate its satisfaction. A further predicate would need the STR's urgent-submission classification during the blackout and evidence of direct JFIU contact by at least one listed method.

The retained text does not specify the operational use of an e-Cert. The certificate fact must remain unknown until that requirement and the submission evidence establish it; possession alone cannot be substituted.

The formal language lacks timestamps and event quantifiers. The proposals therefore declare explicit temporal and event-history facts whose underlying evidence must be assessed externally; no date-only comparison or invented fact value substitutes for that evidence.
A determination that a resubmission obligation is outstanding, overdue or discharged needs additional facts and any applicable JFIU guidance. The trigger model does not answer those questions.
The four listed missing dependencies have no supplied contents. Their implications, the separately provided XML schema, technical test details and subsequent resubmission guidance remain unexamined.

No prior models were supplied for a missing-schema challenge. Internal inspection identified consequential distinctions between channel and method, submission and contact, report and submission event, original event and resubmission, and calendar date and launch instant. The second proposal addresses the event-history distinction without asserting an unsupported rival interpretation.

Retain the blackout urgent-contact exception as a separate conditional instruction: for an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout, contact the JFIU by the stated email, phone or fax. Neither proposed result tests performance of this instruction. Direct contact does not by itself establish successful filing, and the post-launch exclusive-channel rule is not applied within the blackout.

The precise operational meaning of the e-Cert requirement remains unresolved. The first proposal is conditional on its explicit certificate-availability assumption; it cannot establish that mere availability suffices under technical requirements absent from the supplied text.

The permitted expression fragment cannot compare timestamps directly. Temporal facts must be established externally with the launch time and governing timezone preserved; a date-only comparison would lose a consequential boundary.

The resubmission trigger is representable, but timely discharge is not specified sufficiently to model: the supplied source gives no deadline and refers to further JFIU guidance. What timing and completion evidence does that guidance require?
The four dependency identifiers have no supplied contents or source hashes. No requirements from those missing materials, the separate XML schema or further JFIU guidance have been inferred.
